A field guide to an inhabited world

Harpies

Eight distinct birdlike monster-girl concepts designed as part of Minecraft’s ecology: creatures with habitats, instincts, routines, and memorable ways to interact with the player—not a separate civilization.

I · HarpiesII · Bullywugs & Mucus ToadsIII · NekomataIV · KitsuneV · LamiaVI · ArachneVII · CentaursVIII · MerfolkIX · Slimes
Design philosophy

Wildlife first. Relationship second.

Harpies should make the world feel more alive without turning it into a populated fantasy society. Most are ambient encounters; only a small number need to become persistent, relationship-aware individuals.

  • Ecology before questsHabitats, food, nesting, weather, and time of day shape behaviour.
  • Friendly isn't obedientA familiar harpy still has its instincts and needs.
  • Rare encounters matterLow spawn rates make a remembered individual feel special.
  • Journal without forced namingRecord species and observations; name or track an individual only after a meaningful bond.

Species catalogue

Browse by ecological niche or search for a behaviour. The categories are practical design groupings, not rigid biological taxonomy.

8 species
Settlement & gardenAmbient · approachable

Sparrow Harpy

HabitatVillages, gardens, farms, and player-built homes

TemperamentCurious, sociable, easily startled

Ecology & behaviourBathes in water or dust, sings from rooftops, follows friendly mobs, and visits farms to ask for seeds or bread. May snatch small items.

Player interactionLeave a birdbath, plant crops, and offer seeds or bread. A safe, lively home may encourage repeat visits.

Pitch notesSmall flier. Takes sand and water baths, sings, and sometimes flies alongside any friendly mob. Waits beside farms to ask for seeds and bread.

DangerLow; usually flees rather than fights.

Open landTerritorial · grounded

Ostrich Harpy

HabitatPlains, savannas, and other open ground

TemperamentWary, proud, territorial

Ecology & behaviourRuns quickly, patrols familiar ground, and uses warning displays before charging when a nest or territory is threatened.

Player interactionKeep a respectful distance, avoid rushing the nest, and let trust build gradually.

Pitch notesFlightless and fast on land. Hurts when angered and is extremely territorial, but loyal when cared for.

DangerHigh when angered; can seriously injure an unprepared player.

Open sky & cliffsSkittish · wide-ranging

Albatross Harpy

HabitatCoasts, sea cliffs, and broad open spaces suitable for landing

TemperamentIndependent, cautious, hard to approach

Ecology & behaviourSoars over long distances, avoids cramped or hilly landing sites, and may swoop down to steal food from an inventory.

Player interactionWatch from a distance and leave food in a clear, open spot if you want to observe one.

Pitch notesLarge flier that needs a big clearing to land, so it avoids hilly terrain. Skittish: vanishes when approached. Likes to swoop down and steal food items out of the player inventory.

DangerLow direct aggression; theft and sudden fly-bys are the main nuisance.

Coast & open seaSocial · opportunistic

Seagull Harpy

HabitatBeaches, harbours, and isolated rock formations at sea

TemperamentBold, noisy, opportunistic

Ecology & behaviourFollows boats, begs for fish, steals food, and gathers in flocks. Its alluring song around dangerous reefs can lure sailors off course.

Player interactionOffer fish on safe shores; treat unusually dense flocks or distant singing as a possible warning.

Pitch notesSmall coast- and sea-borne harpy. Gathers around rock formations on the open sea singing happy, alluring, siren-like songs that result in shipwrecks. Follows any boat, asks passersby on land for fish, and sometimes swoops down to steal from players.

DangerModerate; the greatest danger comes from misleading songs and hazardous waters.

Forest & nightPredator · mostly solitary

Owl Harpy

HabitatForests and quiet wooded areas, especially after dark

TemperamentPatient, observant, predatory

Ecology & behaviourPerches silently, watches potential prey, and hunts livestock or wild animals such as pigs, sheep, cows, and frogs.

Player interactionOffer meat to encourage a closer approach, and protect livestock if you notice repeated night visits.

Pitch notesLarge nocturnal flier and fierce predator of pigs, sheep, cows and even frogs. Mainly lives in forested areas. Stalks players but is mostly harmless. Hoots at players and comes out when offered a piece of meat, even cooked.

DangerA threat to vulnerable animals; usually avoids a direct fight with the player.

Woodland edge & farmsClever · playful

Crow Harpy

HabitatForests, farms, villages, and places with useful objects

TemperamentCurious, opportunistic, mischievous

Ecology & behaviourSolves simple problems, avoids known traps, imitates sounds, knocks on wood, caches objects, and plays pranks by moving stolen items.

Player interactionTreat encounters as a game: observe what it learns, trade safely, and never leave precious items exposed as bait.

Pitch notesMedium-sized and very intelligent: solves problems, avoids traps, opens doors, knocks on wood. A prankster that steals items out of the player inventory only to drop them further down the road. A hatchling found by the player becomes loyal. Murders of crow harpies gather around farms to scavenge. Imitates noises it hears almost flawlessly.

DangerLow physical danger; its intelligence makes it a persistent nuisance.

RainforestDisplay-focused · rare

Riflebird Harpy

HabitatWarm, dense rainforest with clearings for courtship displays

TemperamentShowy, selective, curious

Ecology & behaviourPerforms elaborate dances, makes musical calls, and sometimes imitates familiar melodies. May lay an unfertilized egg in a suitable nest.

Player interactionGive it room to display and offer food or a valuable gift to invite a closer relationship.

Pitch notesSmall rainforest dweller. Dances to impress mates, sometimes in front of players for affection. Given diamonds, emeralds or any type of food, it bonds and sometimes lays unfertilized eggs; it does not mind the player taking them. Its songs sound like pop songs (Michael Jackson reference).

DangerLow; most encounters are about display, curiosity, and courtship behaviour.

Nether & fireRare · reborn

Phoenix Harpy

HabitatNether environments and places shaped by intense heat

TemperamentFierce, magical, intensely imprinted

Ecology & behaviourOn death, leaves ashes that can be collected. Placed in or near a fire, the ashes develop into a tiny phoenix harpy that grows over time. After rebirth, it imprints on the first thing it sees.

Player interactionProtect the ashes, choose a safe rebirth site, and be present when the hatchling emerges. Bonded phoenixes may resist ghast fireballs; their magical tears can grant regeneration.

Pitch notesMedium-sized, Nether-occupying fierce fighter. Reborn after being slain and burning to ashes; a reborn phoenix imprints on the first thing it sees, so enemies can become friends. Its magical tears heal players with the Regeneration effect. If friends with a player, it deflects all ghast fireballs.

DangerHigh during encounters; powerful and difficult to predict until bonded.

No harpies match that search. Try another term or habitat.

Shared mechanics worth considering

A small set of reusable systems can support very different species without making every encounter a complicated simulation.

1. Ambient populationMost harpies are temporary or lightly simulated. Only nearby, notable, or bonded individuals need persistent memory.
2. Nests & eggsNests are habitat objects. Eggs are unfertilised by default (riflebird, sparrow). Fertilised eggs come only from sharing a bed with a harpy who trusts you: she builds a nest and lays a clutch (see Nests, hatchlings & companions).
3. Individual bondsTrack a relationship only for a deliberately bonded harpy. A field journal can record species discoveries without assigning every creature a personal name.

Design decisions log

Archived from the original pitch conversation (ChatGPT brainstorm), added 2026-10-16. Recorded as stated. Species details from the pitch appear as "Pitch notes" on each card above.

UniverseBuild on the “monmusu” / “Everyday with Monster Girls” universe, in the spirit of Grimoire of Gaia and the Monster Girl Encyclopedia setting.
ToneTake the erotic fantasy horror of those sources and make it mainly fantasy.
World integrationMinecraft biomes should spawn monster girls. Each species belongs to the biomes in its habitat.

Bond pathways named in the pitch

  • Ostrich: loyal when cared for.
  • Owl: comes out when offered meat, even cooked.
  • Crow: a hatchling found by the player becomes loyal.
  • Phoenix: imprints on the first thing it sees after rebirth, so enemies can become friends; a friend deflects all ghast fireballs.
  • Riflebird: bonds when given diamonds, emeralds or any type of food; may lay unfertilized eggs the player can take.

Scope & open questions

  • Harpies are the starting point and a small sliver of the wider vision.
  • Open: what this mod does differently from existing monster-girl mods is undecided.
  • Hatchlings (2026-10-18): a harpy who spent the night beside someone she trusts builds a woven nest with a fertilised egg (since 2026-10-19 a clutch of two to four, each hatchling in a random colour) (it cracks in four stages, about a day, assets by tools/gen_harpy_eggs.py); a tiny hatchling harpy comes out (eight models, tools/gen_hatchlings.py) and grows up in five days. Decided 2026-10-18: with the frogs and toads joining, the mod is called MonsterGirls (id monstergirls, renamed from harpies on 2026-10-18).
  • Open: the pitch builds on the monmusu universe, while the design philosophy above says harpies are ecology, not a separate civilization. Not yet reconciled.

Ostrich Harpy — concept sheet

Added 2026-10-16. Proud, wary, and very fast. This sheet is generated from the actual model (tools/gen_ostrich_harpy.py), so the turnaround below is a render of what is in the game files, not a separate illustration. Behaviour notes are design proposals that follow the species card above and the original pitch.

Colour variants, left to right: common ostrich (male), hen, emu, cassowary, rhea. Texture-only: same model and animations.

Top: front, 3/4, side, back (idle); running; warning display; kick; brooding. Bottom: composed default, display (hiss + angry brows), kick, blink, display from the side.

SilhouetteThe tallest and sturdiest harpy: about 2.3 blocks. Long, heavily muscled legs, a broad chest, a slender waist, a long neck, a big white tail fan and small black-and-white wings. She does not fly, so she is built for power, not lightness.
TemperamentComposed and haughty by default: level brows, a flat mouth, long lashes. The face only turns hostile (angry brows, hiss) once the display starts.
ScaleModel height is about 36 units. Suggested hitbox 0.9 × 2.3. Sparrow and crow render smaller than this, so she should loom over them.

Visual design

  • Colour schemeTaken from a real ostrich: black and white plumage, pinkish-grey bare skin, a blue-grey accent for the neck, grey-brown downy head feathers.
  • HairDusty taupe and hip-length: land harpies let their hair grow. Long locks frame the face and the back hair flows to the hips, with a fluffy crown (like an ostrich’s head down) and two black-and-white plumes tucked behind one ear.
  • FaceBig round dark-brown eyes with long, sweeping lashes; strong level brows; pinkish-grey skin with a rosy blush.
  • BuildA broad ribcage with a fuller bust, a slender waist, wide hips. Big upper thighs, a smaller lower thigh and a bulging calf give the legs a visible muscle shape.
  • Wings & tailSmall vestigial wings: black coverts, short white plumes that hang like a cape at rest and fan wide in the display. A seven-plume white tail fan lifts and shakes when she is angry.
  • OutfitBlack feather bodice, near-black leather belt with bone and blue-grey beads, a short grey-brown cloth apron with a white zig-zag border (open at the sides so the thighs show), leather arm wraps with white feather cuffs, a bone pendant and a blue-grey beaded choker.
  • FeetPink-grey scaled legs ending in two-toed feet: one big inner toe with a heavy black claw, one small outer toe. No hind toe.

  • Taupe hair #7a6a5c

Colour variants

  • Common ostrich (default)Black bodice, white plumes, pinkish-grey skin and legs, blue-grey beads.
  • HenThe female ostrich: grey-brown plumage with pale grey-brown plumes, sand-coloured cloth, rust beads.
  • EmuShaggy dark-brown plumage, pale blue-grey neck skin, orange eyes, dark grey legs, emu-egg green cloth and beads.
  • CassowaryGlossy blue-black hair and plumage, vivid blue neck with red wattles, red-brown eyes, pale yellow-grey legs, midnight cloth with red beads. A casque (the crest on its head) would be a model change, not a recolour, so it is not included.
  • RheaSoft grey plumage, pale plumes, pale blue-grey cloth.
  • Filesostrich_harpy_hen.png, _emu.png, _cassowary.png, _rhea.png; the default stays ostrich_harpy.png. Picking a variant per biome or per spawn is a Java-side decision, the same way the sparrow does it.

Expressions

  • Composed (default)Level brows, flat mouth. Proud, unreadable, a little aloof.
  • Warning display (built)Mouth open in a hiss, brows dragged down and in. Shown through the whole display and, with a closed mouth, during the kick.
  • Blink (built)Eyelids slide out for a moment, like the other harpies.
  • PlannedAlert (wide eyes, brows up) for the moment she first spots you; content (soft eyes, small smile) once you are bonded.

Animations (built)

  • idle / walkUpright, scanning head turns; long unhurried strides.
  • runThe charge: long strides, body leaning forward, wings out for balance, hair streaming back, brows angry.
  • displayWings thrown wide and quivering, head lowered, hissing, alternating stomps, tail fan raised and shaking.
  • kickWind-up, then a straight-legged thrust forward with wings flared. The signature attack.
  • broodSitting on the nest with legs folded under her, head slowly scanning the territory, slow blinks.

Territory & escalation (proposed)

  • Home groundShe patrols a radius around a nest and returns to it. Nests are habitat objects; eggs are unfertilised by default.
  • Stage 1 — watchA stranger enters the outer ring: she stops, turns, stands tall. No hostility yet.
  • Stage 2 — displayCloser, or near the nest: the display animation plus hiss and stomps. This is the readable warning.
  • Stage 3 — charge, then kickIf the player keeps closing in, she runs them down and kicks for heavy damage and knockback. She disengages once they leave the territory.
  • NeverShe does not chase far outside her territory, and a bonded player never triggers any stage.

Relationship (proposed)

  • Hostile → wary → tolerant → loyalTrust builds slowly, as the species card says: keep a respectful distance, stay away from the nest, leave food at the edge of her territory and back off.
  • What costs trustRushing the nest, taking an egg, hitting her.
  • LoyalBonded individuals follow and guard the player, patrol around them, and run attackers down. Loyalty is earned by care, not obedience: she still defends her own territory and nest.

Model facts

  • 145 cubes, 27 bones, 256×256 texture at 4 texels per unit (same density as the sparrow and crow).
  • Same bone names as the other harpies, so shared animation code works: head, wing_r/l, wing_tip_r/l, leg_r/l, tail, hair_back, …
  • Expression parts eyelids, mouth, brows sit just inside the face and slide out through position animations.
  • Files: ostrich_harpy.geo.json, ostrich_harpy.animation.json, ostrich_harpy.png under src/main/resources/assets/monstergirls/.

Open questions

  • Should the female/male colouring split (grey-brown vs black-and-white) be two variants of the same mob?
  • How far should the kick knock a player back, and how much damage on each difficulty?
  • What should she accept as an offering at the territory edge (wheat, melon, something new)?

Relationships (shared by every family)

Updated 2026-10-19. Every MonsterGirls family uses the same relationship core; each volume only changes how trust is won, what she gives back and how she bears young. The new families (volumes III to IX) are in their own guides.

AffectionEach monster girl remembers every player separately. Feeding, petting and her family's own bond action raise it; hurting her lowers it. /monstergirls bonds lists everyone nearby.
SitRight-click any monster girl with a plain stick to make her sit; again to let her get up.
Sharing a bedAt high friendship (25) she may join you in bed: once a night she decides, one in three at 25, certain at 100. Sleep through the night and she is expecting.
ExpectingA pregnancy lasts one in-game day. Her belly rounds out as it goes on (the model shows it).
Born devotedHer young are born devoted to the player who fathered them (full affection) and never share that player's bed.
PresentsAt high friendship every family brings presents of its own kind.
BondAffectionWhat it means
Wild0Keeps her distance; her species' instincts decide everything.
Curious3+Lets you come close and watches what you do.
Fond10+Follows you a little way, accepts petting, stops fleeing.
High friendship25+May join you in bed at night (one night in three, more the fonder she is) and brings presents.
Devoted60+The family's devoted perk unlocks (see each guide).
Full devotion100The most there is. Every daughter feels this for the player who fathered her.

Nests, hatchlings & companions

Updated 2026-10-19. What a harpy does once you have won her over. All of this is in the game.

Mating & the nest

  • BedAt high friendship (25) she may hop into your bed and lie down beside you (one night in three at 25, every night at 100). Sleep through the night and she is expecting.
  • ExpectingOne in-game day. Her belly rounds out as the day goes on (a belly bone added to every adult model).
  • Nest & clutchWhen her time comes she picks a spot (her home if it will do, otherwise a dry, solid spot nearby), weaves a nest for a while, and lays a clutch of two to four fertilised eggs in it. The nest becomes her home, so she broods on it at night.
  • HatchlingsThe eggs crack over about a day and hatch one hatchling each: her species, each in a random colour of it. Hatchlings grow up in five days.
  • Born devotedEvery hatchling is devoted to the player who fathered the clutch: full affection, and her species' own bond on top (a crow treats that player as her companion, a phoenix is imprinted, an ostrich is loyal). A daughter never shares her father's bed.

Companions

  • SitRight-click any harpy with a stick: she sits down (a new sit pose) until you do it again.
  • CrowAt high friendship she sometimes brings raw iron or raw gold, a diamond in rare cases. With a chest, barrel or hopper nearby that already holds that item, she drops it in there instead of handing it over.
  • RiflebirdBrings seeds straight into your inventory (now and then a torchflower seed or pitcher pod), on top of her unfertilised eggs.
  • OwlBrings food from the night's hunt: rabbit, chicken, cod, berries, apples.
  • Seagull & albatrossBring what the sea gave up: fish, kelp, ink sacs, prismarine, turtle scutes, a nautilus shell, very rarely a heart of the sea.
  • PhoenixHer warmth heals the player she imprinted on: half a heart every two seconds within eight blocks.
  • SparrowRoosts on a hopper and lays an unfertilised Sparrow Egg into it every five to ten minutes. Sparrow eggs can be eaten raw and bake into cakes and pumpkin pies like hen eggs (they also count as eggs for other mods: c:eggs).
